misconceptions.description: Treating interpretability and explainability as synonyms
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses the two terms interchangeably without distinction
misconceptions.feedback: Interpretability is a property of the model (auditable by structure). Explainability is a property of an explanation surface around a possibly opaque model. The two can be present independently.

misconceptions.description: Treating SHAP or LIME outputs as automatically constituting a meaningful explanation
misconceptions.trigger: learner provides raw feature attributions to a denied applicant as the legal explanation
misconceptions.feedback: Meaningful explanations are faithful, actionable, and contextually appropriate. Raw feature attributions can fail on actionability and may inappropriately surface protected-attribute proxies.

misconceptions.description: Believing post-hoc explanation methods reveal the model's actual mechanism
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites SHAP output as proof of why the model made a decision
misconceptions.feedback: Post-hoc methods approximate model behavior locally. They can be wrong. A satisfying explanation is not necessarily a faithful explanation.

misconceptions.description: Assuming black-box models are always more accurate than interpretable alternatives
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues 'we need a black box for accuracy' without testing interpretable baselines
misconceptions.feedback: Rudin (2019) argues that for high-stakes decisions, inherently interpretable models are often competitive in accuracy and dominate on auditability. Test before assuming.
